report.answer: Middleware composition in Hono is implemented in src/compose.ts, which exports a koa-compose-style `compose()` function that turns an array of [handler, params] middleware tuples into a single dispatcher using recursive `dispatch(i)`/`next()` calls, with built-in error and not-found handling. It is invoked from src/hono-base.ts's request dispatch path (~line 450, `Hono.prototype.dispatch` / fetch handling): matched routes are composed via `compose(matchResult[0], this.errorHandler, this.#notFoundHandler)`, with a fast-path skip when only one handler matches (line 429-430). It's also reused directly for single-route handler wrapping (line 224-226) and by src/middleware/combine/index.ts to combine multiple middlewares into one.

report.answer: Errors propagate through two nested layers. Inside src/compose.ts's dispatch(i), each middleware call is wrapped in try/catch: if a thrown value is `instanceof Error` and an `onError` handler was passed to compose(), it's handled inline (`context.error = err; res = await onError(err, context)`, `isError=true`) and composition continues; otherwise the error is rethrown up the dispatch promise chain. Outside compose, src/hono-base.ts's `#dispatch()` wraps the `await composed(c)` call (multi-handler path, ~line 452-465) and the direct single-handler call (~line 429-445) in an outer try/catch that calls `#handleError(err, c)` (line 399-403), which invokes `this.errorHandler(err, c)` only if `err instanceof Error`, else rethrows; the default errorHandler (line 35) special-cases HTTPException-like errors via `getResponse()` else returns a generic response. `this.errorHandler`/`app.onError()` (line 271-274) is the single handler passed both into compose() and used by #handleError, so both layers funnel to the same user-configured handler, but compose's inline catch lets later middleware still run after an error is absorbed, while the outer catch is the final safety net (e.g. for the 'Context is not finalized' error compose can throw).

verified.summary: compose.ts dispatch(i) catches per-middleware errors, calls onError if Error, else rethrows
